intro: This unit is about one family. The Torah says God told Abraham and Sarah to leave home. They went to a new land. Their family grew. Isaac and Rebekah came next. Then Jacob, Leah and Rachel. Then Joseph and his brothers.

Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of its family. Jewish families read these stories every year. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what the stories mean to the people who read them. We do not decide if they are true. We listen and we learn.

By the end, you will be able to tell how Abraham and Sarah welcomed guests. You will know Jacob's dream and his new name. You will know how Joseph forgave his brothers. And you will know how the twelve tribes got their names.
bigQuestion: What do the Torah's stories of Abraham's family say about promises, kindness and forgiving?

God promises Abram a family as many as the stars
Three travelers come, and Abraham runs to feed them
Isaac is born; his name means "he laughs"
Rebekah waters ten camels at the well and marries Isaac
Twins are born: Esau and Jacob
Jacob dreams of a ladder to the sky
Jacob marries Leah and Rachel and has twelve sons and a daughter
Jacob wrestles all night and gets the name Israel
Joseph's brothers sell him, and he is taken to Egypt
Joseph becomes Pharaoh's top helper and saves food
Joseph forgives his brothers, and the family moves to Egypt

the man the Torah says left home for a new land; Jewish tradition calls him the first of the family
a person who comes to visit your home
a story Jewish teachers tell to add to a Torah story
the son of Abraham and Sarah; his Hebrew name means "he laughs"
the new name the Torah says Jacob was given; his family became the people of Israel
a very big family group; the Torah names twelve tribes of Israel
to stop being angry at someone for what they did

test.why: A midrash says Abraham's tent was open on all sides so any guest could come in.

test.q: Who were Isaac's mother and father?
test.why: Isaac was the son of Sarah and Abraham.

test.q: What did Rebekah do for the stranger's camels?
test.why: Genesis 24 says Rebekah drew water for the man and all ten of his camels.
Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twins, Esau and Jacob.

write.prompt: Pick one person from this unit: Abraham (Genesis 18), Rebekah (Genesis 24), Jacob (Genesis 28) or Joseph (Genesis 45). Draw or write one kind or brave thing the Torah says they did. Then tell what Jewish tradition says we can learn from it.
tips: Say which person and story you picked, like "Abraham, Genesis 18."
Say "the Torah says" when you tell what happened.
Say "Jewish tradition says" when you tell what the story teaches.
Use two words from the unit, like guest, promise or forgive.

title: Abraham, Sarah and Their Family

chapters.title: Abraham and Sarah Go to a New Land
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Torah say Abraham and Sarah did when they left home, and how did they treat people?

story.title: Three Travelers in the Hot Sun
story.kicker: It is the hottest part of the day, and an old man runs to greet three strangers.
paragraphs: The sun is high. The sand is hot. An old man named Abraham sits at the door of his tent. He is resting in the shade. The Torah says he looks up. Three travelers are standing there.
Abraham does not wait. The Torah says he runs to them. He bows low. "Please stay," he says. "Rest under the tree. Let me bring water for your feet. Let me bring you bread."

Abraham hurries to the tent. "Sarah," he says, "quick, make bread!" Then he runs to the animals. He picks a calf for the meal. He brings milk and cheese too. He stands by the travelers while they eat.

The travelers have news. They say, "Next year, Sarah will have a son." Sarah is listening at the tent door. She laughs. She is very old. Can this be true? Jewish tradition tells this story every year.
story.think: Abraham ran to help strangers on a hot day. What do you do when a guest comes to your home?

lessons.title: Go to a New Land
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God told Abraham and Sarah to leave home and go to a new land, and they went.
reading: Abraham and Sarah lived in a place far away. Their first names were Abram and Sarai. The Torah says God spoke to Abram. God said, "Leave your land. Go to a land I will show you."
Abram did not know where he was going. He went anyway. Sarai went with him. So did his nephew Lot. They took their tents and their sheep. They walked a long way to a new *land*.
The new land was called Canaan. Jewish tradition says this is the land of Israel. Abraham and Sarah lived there in tents. They moved from place to place.

words.d: a place where people live; the Torah says Abraham went to a new land called Canaan

look.title: Go From Your Land
look.text: Now the LORD said unto Abram: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee.
look.prompt: "Get thee out" is an old way to say "go." What three things does the story say Abram had to leave?

check.q: What does the Torah say God told Abram to do?
choices: Leave his land and go to a new one
check.why: Genesis 12 says God told Abram to leave his land and go to a land God would show him.

check.q: Who went with Abram on the trip?
check.why: Sarai, his wife, and Lot, his nephew, went with him. Noah and Joseph are in other stories.

check.q: What was the new land called?
check.why: The land was called Canaan. Jewish tradition calls it the land of Israel.

lessons.title: A Promise of a Big Family
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God promised Abraham and Sarah a very big family.
reading: Abraham and Sarah had no children. They were getting old. The Torah says God made them a *promise*. God said, "Your family will be big. It will be as many as the stars."
The story says God told Abram to look up at the night sky. Try to count the stars! You cannot. That is how big the family would be.
God gave them new names, the story says. Abram became Abraham. Sarai became Sarah. Jewish tradition says the new names were part of the promise.

words.d: something you say you will do, and then you do it
the man the Torah says left home for a new land; his first name was Abram

look.title: Count the Stars
look.text: Picture a dark night far from the city. There are no street lights. Look up. Stars fill the whole sky. Small ones, bright ones, more and more. The Torah says God told Abram his family would be as many as the stars.
look.prompt: Why do you think the story uses stars to talk about a big family?

check.q: What did God promise Abraham, in the story?
check.why: The Torah says God promised Abraham a family as many as the stars.

check.q: What was Sarah's name before it was Sarah?
check.why: Sarai became Sarah. Rebekah and Rachel are other women in the Torah.

check.q: What did the story tell Abram to look at?
check.why: Genesis 15 says God told Abram to look at the stars and try to count them.

lessons.title: Three Visitors
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Abraham ran to feed three strangers who came to his tent.
reading: One hot day, three travelers came by. Abraham did not know them. The Torah says he ran to meet them. He bowed. He asked them to rest and eat.
Abraham and Sarah made a big meal. Bread, milk, cheese and meat. Abraham did not sit down. He stood by his *guests* while they ate.
The guests had a message. Sarah would have a baby boy. Sarah laughed. She was very old. Jewish tradition says her laugh became the baby's name.

words.d: a person who comes to visit your home

look.title: He Ran to Meet Them
look.text: The Torah says Abraham looked up and saw three men standing near him. He ran from the door of his tent to meet them. He bowed down to the ground.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 18:2, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Abraham ran. He did not walk. What does that tell you about how he felt about guests?

check.q: How many travelers came to Abraham's tent?
check.why: Genesis 18 says three men came. Abraham ran to meet them.

check.q: What did Abraham do when he saw the travelers?
check.why: The Torah says Abraham ran to meet them and asked them to stay and eat.

check.q: What news did the guests bring?
choices: Abraham would get a new tent
check.why: The guests said Sarah would have a baby boy. Sarah laughed.

lessons.title: Kindness to Strangers
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish tradition says Abraham's tent was open on all sides so every guest could come in.
reading: A *stranger* is a person you do not know. Abraham did not know the three men. He helped them anyway. Jewish tradition says this is a big lesson.
An old Jewish story says Abraham's tent was open on all four sides. A guest could walk in from any way. No one had to go around. The story is a *midrash*. A midrash is a story that adds to the Torah.
Jewish families still welcome guests. On Shabbat, many families invite people to eat. They call it welcoming guests. It is a way to be like Abraham and Sarah.

words.d: a person you do not know yet
a story Jewish teachers tell to add to a Torah story

look.title: A Tent With Four Doors
look.text: Picture a tent in the desert. Most tents have one door. This tent has a door on every side. Front, back, left and right. A traveler from any road can see a way in. Jewish tradition tells this story about Abraham's tent.
look.prompt: Why would a tent with four doors be good for guests? What is one way our classroom could be like that tent?

check.q: What is a stranger?
choices: A person you do not know
check.why: A stranger is someone you do not know yet. Abraham helped strangers.

check.q: What does the midrash say about Abraham's tent?
choices: It was open on all sides
check.why: The midrash says the tent was open on all sides so any guest could come in.

check.q: What do many Jewish families do on Shabbat to be like Abraham?
check.why: Welcoming guests to a meal is a way Jewish families follow Abraham and Sarah.

lessons.title: Isaac Is Born
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Sarah had a son named Isaac, and his name means "he laughs."
reading: The Torah says the promise came true. Sarah had a baby boy. They named him *Isaac*. In Hebrew, his name is Yitzchak. It means "he laughs."
Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me." Everyone who heard the news would laugh with her. Abraham and Sarah were very old. The story says Abraham was one hundred.
Jewish families read this story on Rosh Hashanah. That is the Jewish New Year. They hear how Isaac was born.

words.d: the son of Abraham and Sarah; his Hebrew name means "he laughs"

look.title: Big Numbers in the Story
rows: Travelers who came to the tent
Sarah's age when Isaac was born
Abraham's age when Isaac was born
look.cite: Genesis 17:17, 18:2 and 21:5, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Why do you think Sarah laughed?

check.q: What does the name Isaac mean?
check.why: Isaac, or Yitzchak, means "he laughs." Sarah laughed when she heard the news.

check.q: Who were Isaac's mother and father?
check.why: Isaac was the son of Sarah and Abraham. Rachel and Jacob come later.

check.q: When do Jewish families read the story of Isaac's birth?
check.why: The story of Isaac's birth is read on Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year.

lessons.title: Rebekah at the Well
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Rebekah gave water to a stranger and his camels, and she became Isaac's wife.
reading: Isaac grew up. Abraham sent a helper to find Isaac a wife. The helper took ten *camels*. He stopped at a well. A well is a deep hole with water in it.
A girl named Rebekah came to the well. The helper asked for a drink. Rebekah gave him water. Then she said, "I will get water for your camels too." Ten camels drink a lot!
The helper knew she was kind. Rebekah went with him. She married Isaac. Jewish tradition says Rebekah was kind like Abraham.

words.d: a big desert animal with a hump that can go a long time without water
a deep hole in the ground where people get water

look.title: Water for the Camels
look.text: Picture a well with a bucket on a rope. A tired man stands next to ten camels. A girl lowers the bucket. She pulls it up. She pours. Then she lowers it again. And again. The Torah says Rebekah did this until all the camels had drunk.
look.prompt: Rebekah did not have to water the camels. Why do you think she did it?

check.q: Where did the helper meet Rebekah?
check.why: Genesis 24 says the helper met Rebekah at a well.

check.q: What did Rebekah give the camels?
check.why: Rebekah drew water for the man and for all ten camels.

check.q: Who did Rebekah marry?
check.why: Rebekah became Isaac's wife. Abraham was his father and Lot was his cousin.

lessons.title: The First of the Family
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first mother and father of the Jewish people.
reading: Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of the family. In Hebrew, Abraham is called Avraham Avinu. That means "Abraham our father." Sarah is Sarah Imenu, "Sarah our mother."
Isaac and Rebekah come next. Then their children. Then their children's children. Jewish tradition says the whole Jewish people is one big *family*.
Jewish prayers name Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Many prayers name Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel and Leah too. The story of the family goes on.

words.d: people who belong together; Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of its family

look.title: The Family Grows
look.cite: Genesis 21 and 25, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Isaac and Rebekah had two sons. Who do you think they were? The next chapter will tell you.

check.q: What does Avraham Avinu mean?
check.why: Avinu means "our father." Jewish tradition calls Abraham the father of the family.

check.q: Who does Jewish tradition call the first mother of the family?
check.why: Sarah is called Sarah Imenu, "Sarah our mother." Rebekah and Rachel came after her.

check.q: Which three men are named in many Jewish prayers?
check.why: Jewish prayers name Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of the family.

review.q: What does the Torah say God told Abram and Sarai to do?
choices: Leave home and go to a new land
review.why: Genesis 12 says God told Abram to leave his land and go to a land God would show him.

review.q: The story says Abraham's family would be as many as what?
review.why: Genesis 15 says the family would be as many as the stars in the sky.

review.q: What did Abraham do when three strangers came?
choices: He ran to give them food
review.why: Genesis 18 says Abraham ran to meet them and gave them a big meal.

choices: A story that adds to a Torah story
review.why: A midrash is a story Jewish teachers tell to add to the Torah. One says Abraham's tent was open on all sides.

review.q: What does the name Isaac mean?
review.why: Isaac, or Yitzchak, means "he laughs." Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a son.

review.q: What kind thing did Rebekah do at the well?
choices: She gave water to a man and his camels
review.why: Genesis 24 says Rebekah gave water to the helper and to all his camels.

chapters.title: Jacob, Rachel, Leah and Joseph
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Torah say happened to Jacob's family, and how did the twelve tribes get their names?

story.title: A Ladder to the Sky
story.kicker: A young man sleeps on a stone and dreams of a ladder that goes all the way up.
paragraphs: It is night. A young man named Jacob is far from home. He is alone. He has no bed. The Torah says he puts a stone under his head. He lies down on the ground. He falls asleep.
Jacob dreams. In the dream, there is a ladder. Its bottom is on the earth. Its top reaches the sky. Angels are going up the ladder. Angels are coming down. Up and down, up and down.
In the dream, the story says, God speaks to Jacob. "I am with you. I will keep you safe. I will bring you back to this land." It is the same promise God made to Abraham.
Jacob wakes up. He is amazed. "God was here," he says, "and I did not know it!" He sets up the stone. He names the place Beth-el. That means "house of God."
story.think: Jacob was alone and far from home. How do you think the dream made him feel?

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Isaac and Rebekah had twin sons, Jacob and Esau, who did not get along.
reading: Isaac and Rebekah had *twins*. Twins are two babies born together. The first was Esau. He was red and hairy. The second was Jacob. He was holding Esau's heel.
The boys grew up very different. Esau liked to hunt outside. Jacob liked to stay near the tents. The Torah says the brothers had a big fight over a blessing.
Esau was angry. Jacob had to leave home. He went far away to his uncle Laban. He did not see his brother for a long, long time.

words.d: two babies born together from the same mother; Jacob and Esau were twins
Jacob's twin brother; the Torah says he was born first

look.title: Two Very Different Brothers
look.text: Picture two boys who are twins. One has red hair all over his arms. He carries a bow and runs to the fields. The other stays by the tents and cooks a pot of red stew. They are brothers, but they are not the same.
look.prompt: The Torah says the twins were very different. What is one way you are different from someone in your family?

check.q: Who were Jacob and Esau's parents?
check.why: Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twin sons, Esau and Jacob.

check.q: Which twin was born first?
check.why: Esau was born first. Jacob came second, holding Esau's heel.

check.q: Why did Jacob leave home?
choices: He wanted to see the sea
His brother was angry with him
check.why: After the fight over the blessing, Esau was angry, so Jacob went to his uncle Laban.

lessons.title: The Ladder Dream
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob dreamed of a ladder to the sky with angels going up and down.
reading: On his trip, Jacob slept outside. He used a stone for a pillow. The Torah says he had a dream. He saw a *ladder*. It went from the ground to the sky.
Angels went up the ladder. Angels came down. In the dream, God made Jacob a promise. "I am with you. I will bring you back home."
Jacob woke up. He named the place Beth-el. Beth-el means "house of God." Jewish tradition says the dream showed Jacob he was not alone.

words.d: a tall set of steps you climb; Jacob dreamed of one that reached the sky
the name Jacob gave the place where he dreamed; it means "house of God"

look.title: A Ladder Set Up on the Earth
look.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
look.prompt: "Ascending" means going up. "Descending" means going down. Show with your hand what the angels were doing.

check.q: What did Jacob see in his dream?
check.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of a ladder from the earth to the sky. The boat and rainbow are in Noah's story.

check.q: What did Jacob use for a pillow?
check.why: The Torah says Jacob put a stone under his head and went to sleep.

check.q: What does Beth-el mean?
check.why: Beth-el means "house of God." Jacob named the place after his dream. "He laughs" is Isaac's name.

lessons.title: Rachel and Leah
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob worked many years for Laban and married both Leah and Rachel.
reading: Jacob came to his uncle Laban. Laban had two daughters. Leah was the older one. *Rachel* was the younger one. Jacob met Rachel at a well. He loved her.
Jacob said, "I will work for you seven years. Then let me marry Rachel." Laban said yes. But at the wedding, Laban gave him *Leah* instead. Jacob was tricked!
Jacob worked seven more years. Then he married Rachel too. In those days, a man could have more than one wife. Both Leah and Rachel are called mothers of the family.

words.d: Laban's younger daughter; the Torah says Jacob loved her and met her at a well
Laban's older daughter; the Torah says Jacob married her first

look.title: Jacob Works for Laban
rows: Years Jacob worked before he married Leah
More years he worked for Rachel
look.unit: years, as the Torah tells it
look.prompt: The Torah says seven years felt like a few days to Jacob because he loved Rachel. What makes time feel fast for you?

check.q: Who was Laban?
check.why: Laban was Rebekah's brother, so he was Jacob's uncle. Esau was his twin.

check.q: How many years did Jacob first work to marry Rachel?
check.why: Genesis 29 says Jacob worked seven years, and then seven more.

check.q: Who did Laban give Jacob at the first wedding?
check.why: Laban gave him Leah, the older daughter. Jacob married Rachel later.

lessons.title: A New Name: Israel
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob wrestled all night with a stranger and got a new name, Israel.
reading: Many years went by. Jacob went home with his big family. He was afraid to see Esau. The night before, he was alone by a river.
The Torah says a stranger came. They *wrestled* all night. To wrestle is to grab and push and not let go. At dawn, the stranger said, "Let me go." Jacob said, "Not until you bless me."
The stranger gave Jacob a new name: *Israel*. The next day, Jacob met Esau. Esau ran to him. They hugged and cried. The brothers made peace.

words.d: to grab and push against someone and not let go
the new name the Torah says Jacob was given; his family became the people of Israel

look.title: Not Jacob, But Israel
look.text: The Torah says the stranger told Jacob: your name will not be Jacob anymore. It will be Israel. You have struggled with God and with people, and you have held on.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 32:29, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Jacob got a new name after he held on all night. What is something hard you kept trying at?

check.q: What new name did Jacob get?
check.why: Genesis 32 says Jacob's new name was Israel. Esau is his brother and Isaac is his father.

check.q: What did Jacob do all night by the river?
check.why: The Torah says Jacob wrestled with a stranger until dawn.

check.q: What happened when Jacob met Esau again?
check.why: Genesis 33 says Esau ran to Jacob, hugged him, and they both cried.

lessons.title: Twelve Sons and Dinah
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob had twelve sons and a daughter, and the twelve tribes are named for his sons.
reading: Jacob had a very big family. The Torah says he had twelve sons. He also had a daughter. Her name was Dinah. Leah and Rachel were mothers of the family.
Some sons were Reuben, Judah, Levi and Joseph. Joseph was Rachel's son. Rachel's other son was Benjamin. He was the youngest of all.
Later, the family grew into a people. Jewish tradition says the people had twelve *tribes*. A tribe is a very big family group. The tribes were named for Jacob's sons.

words.d: a very big family group; the Torah names twelve tribes of Israel
Jacob and Leah's daughter, named in the Torah

look.title: Jacob's Children
look.cite: Genesis 29–30, 35:22–26 and 49:28, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: How many sons did Jacob have? How many tribes? What do you notice?

check.q: How many sons does the Torah say Jacob had?
check.why: Genesis says Jacob had twelve sons. The twelve tribes are named for them.

check.q: Who was Dinah?
check.why: Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah. Rebekah was his mother.

check.q: What is a tribe?
check.why: A tribe is a very big family group. The people of Israel had twelve tribes.

lessons.title: The Coat and the Dreams
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob gave Joseph a special coat, and Joseph's dreams made his brothers jealous.
reading: Jacob loved Joseph very much. The Torah says he gave Joseph a special *coat*. His brothers did not get one. They were *jealous*. To be jealous is to want what someone else has.
Joseph had dreams. In one, his brothers' bundles of wheat bowed to his bundle. In another, the sun, moon and stars bowed to him. Joseph told everyone. His brothers got even more angry.
One day the brothers were far away with the sheep. Jacob sent Joseph to check on them. The brothers saw him coming in his coat.

words.d: the special piece of clothing the Torah says Jacob gave Joseph
wanting what someone else has and feeling upset about it

look.title: Bundles That Bow
look.text: Picture a field at harvest. Wheat is tied in tall bundles. In Joseph's dream, his bundle stands up straight. All his brothers' bundles bend over and bow to it. Joseph tells his brothers the dream. They frown.
look.prompt: What do you think the brothers thought the dream meant? How would you feel if you were a brother?

check.q: What did Jacob give Joseph?
check.why: Genesis 37 says Jacob made Joseph a special coat, and his brothers were jealous.

check.q: What does jealous mean?
check.why: Jealous means wanting what someone else has. The brothers wanted Joseph's coat and their father's love.

check.q: In Joseph's dream, what bowed to his bundle of wheat?
check.why: In the dream, the brothers' bundles bowed to Joseph's bundle. The brothers did not like that.

lessons.title: Joseph in Egypt
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Joseph's brothers sold him, but in Egypt he became a great helper to the king.
reading: The brothers grabbed Joseph. They took his coat. They put him in a deep hole. Then they sold him to travelers going to *Egypt*. They told Jacob that Joseph was dead. Jacob cried and cried.
In Egypt, Joseph worked hard. But he was blamed for something he did not do. He was put in jail. In jail, he told people what their dreams meant.
The king of Egypt was called *Pharaoh*. Pharaoh had a strange dream. Joseph said it meant seven good years, then seven hungry years. Pharaoh made Joseph his top helper. Joseph saved up food.

words.d: a land by a big river where the Torah says Joseph was taken
the name for the king of Egypt

look.title: Pharaoh's Dream
rows: Good years with lots of food
look.prompt: Joseph told Pharaoh to save food in the good years. Why was that a smart plan?

check.q: What did the brothers do to Joseph?
choices: They sold him to travelers going to Egypt
check.why: Genesis 37 says the brothers sold Joseph to travelers who took him to Egypt.

check.q: Who is Pharaoh?
check.why: Pharaoh is the name for the king of Egypt. Joseph became his top helper.

check.q: What did Joseph say Pharaoh's dream meant?
choices: Seven good years, then seven hungry years
Pharaoh would get a new coat
check.why: Joseph said the dream meant seven years with lots of food and seven with little, so Egypt should save up.

lessons.title: Brothers Together Again
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Joseph forgave his brothers, and the whole family moved to Egypt.
reading: The hungry years came. Jacob's family had no food. The brothers went to Egypt to buy some. They stood in front of Joseph. They did not know him. He knew them.
Joseph tested them. Then he could not hold back. He cried. "I am Joseph!" he said. "Is my father still alive?" The brothers were scared. But Joseph said, "Do not be afraid."

Joseph *forgave* his brothers. To forgive is to stop being angry at someone. The whole family moved to Egypt. Jacob saw Joseph again. Jewish tradition says forgiving is one of the big lessons of this story.

words.d: to stop being angry at someone for what they did

look.title: You Meant It for Bad
look.text: The Torah says Joseph told his brothers: you planned something bad for me, but God turned it into something good, so that many people could be kept alive.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 50:20, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Joseph chose to forgive. What is one kind thing you could say to someone who was mean to you?

check.q: Why did the brothers go to Egypt?
check.why: In the hungry years, the brothers went to Egypt to buy food.

check.q: What does forgive mean?
choices: To stop being angry at someone
To go on a long trip
check.why: To forgive is to stop being angry at someone. Joseph forgave his brothers.

check.q: Where did Jacob's whole family go at the end of the story?
check.why: Genesis 46 says Jacob and the whole family moved to Egypt to be near Joseph.

review.q: Who were the twins in this chapter?
review.why: Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twins, Esau and Jacob.

review.q: What did Jacob see in his dream at Beth-el?
review.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of a ladder to the sky with angels going up and down.

review.q: Which two sisters did Jacob marry?
review.why: Jacob married Leah first, then Rachel. They were Laban's daughters.
The Torah says the stranger gave Jacob the name Israel after they wrestled.

review.q: How did the twelve tribes get their names?
review.why: The twelve tribes of Israel are named for the sons of Jacob.

review.q: What did Joseph do when his brothers came to Egypt?
review.why: Genesis 45 says Joseph told them who he was, cried, and told them not to be afraid.
